paragraphs: The hardware interface and integration for the Plant Moisture Detection project were implemented using the arduino_stm32core framework, which is built on the STM32 HAL drivers. The system core clock was set to 72 MHz with a PLL x9 configuration, providing ample resources for the application.

The project utilized an ADC1_IN0 pin connected to a soil moisture sensor for analog soil moisture voltage measurement. This pin was configured as an input pin and used in conjunction with a moving average filter to eliminate sensor measurement noise.

The onboard status LED on PC13 was designed to be active-low, which required careful handling of the logic when evaluating threshold or hysteresis state transitions. The project implemented reliable threshold or hysteresis state evaluation to avoid spurious state switching.

The USB-to-UART Adapter was used for serial telemetry and debug monitoring at 115200 baud. This interface allowed for real-time data exchange between the microcontroller and a host computer, facilitating debugging and monitoring of the system's performance.

Overall, the hardware interface and integration were successful in enabling the Plant Moisture Detection project to function as intended, providing accurate soil moisture measurements and reliable status alerts.
